title: An overview of Apache Flink and Kafka Streams

videos.script: Lesson 12 counted sales per window with Spark, one slice at a time. {{spark}} Two other tools are built to do the same count, and they make different choices. {{two}} Flink is an engine, like Spark. But it handles each sale the moment it arrives, and saves its state while the sales keep flowing. {{flink}} Kafka Streams is not an engine at all. It is a library inside your own Java program. To run it on three machines, you start three copies. {{streams}} In this lesson you write the count both ways. A small Java program for Kafka Streams. A few lines of SQL for Flink. {{code}} Then you look under each one: the topics Kafka Streams creates for itself, and the snapshot Flink takes before it stops. {{under}} By the end, you can say which of the three a team should run, and the answer is rarely about speed. {{end}}
